disagreements.topic: Whether the CEO's 2026 share sales were under a Rule 10b5-1 plan
disagreements.positions: The round-1 supervisor said the CEO's March and June 2026 sales were made under a 10b5-1 plan adopted Mar 3 2026 (it cited a MarketScreener summary). In round 2, agent_3 disagrees, citing the primary Form 4s and Form 144s. The other agents accepted the round-1 correction or did not address it.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3 is right, and the round-1 supervisor's correction was wrong. All of CEO Arash Adam Foroughi's Form 4s for the Mar 11-12 and Jun 10-12 2026 sales have the Rule 10b5-1 box set to false, and none has a plan footnote. His June Form 144s leave the plan-adoption date blank. The Mar 3 2026 plan in the Q1 10-Q belongs to director Maynard Webb (up to 40,000 shares), not to the CEO, and the 10-Q says no other officer or director adopted a plan that quarter. So the CEO's sales (about $51m in June: $14.6m on Jun 10, $25.3m on Jun 11 and $11.2m on Jun 12 at $473.55-516.51, plus March sales) were discretionary open-window sales, made inside the class period (Feb 12-Aug 5 2026). This strengthens the class action's scienter argument a little. It has no direct effect on earnings, so it does not move the ladder.

drivers.label: Advertising revenue (= total revenue since the Apps sale)
drivers.source: Actual quarters: XBRL RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (Q1-25 1,159.0, Q2-25 1,258.8, Q3-25 1,405.0, Q4-25 1,657.9; Q1-26 1,842.4; Q2-26 1,923.7) (src 18); Q3-26 2,184.8 (8-K Ex.99.1 and 10-Q accn 0001751008-26-000069, F7; src 46, 47); Q4-26 guide $2,365-2,395M (src 46); 2024 quarters for the y/y series (src 48, 14, 13); Q4-26 build: Census quarterly e-commerce (src 53, 56), Adobe 2026 holiday forecast (src 54), Sensor Tower Q3 2026 IAP (src 55), Q3 call (src 51); outside forecasts: Zacks consensus sales (src 60), Morgan Stanley 2026-11-05 (src 61), Bank of America 2026-08 (src 62), Jefferies advertiser survey (src 63)
drivers.derivation: Q3 FY2026 actual 2,184.8 (+55.5% y/y). Q4 FY2026 2,426.6, built from the two demand engines (guide $2,365-2,395M is only the cross-check: +2.0% over its midpoint; guidance_check). GAMING 1,959.7 = Q3 gaming ~1,835.2 (84% of 2,184.8) x 1.0678, one quarter of the +30% a year FY2027 gaming path below (the models already live plus the rest of the rollout, which the CEO says is still ahead with no committed cadence, src 51); no extra Q4 seasonal lift is added for gaming: the CFO calls gaming's Q4 'always strong' (src 51), but player spending, which funds game advertisers' budgets, is soft (Sensor Tower: top-10 mobile games' Q3 2026 IAP -3% q/q, src 55). CONSUMER 467.0 = Q3 consumer ~349.6 (16%) x 1.1502 (one quarter of the +75% a year FY2027 consumer path: new advertisers, the CEO 'really ramping up the rate of acquiring new customers', src 51) x 1.1615 holiday lift: U.S. e-commerce Q4 2026 at Adobe's Nov-Dec forecast +6.7% y/y (src 54) on Census Q4 2025 365.4 = 389.9, over the Census Q3 2026 actual 335.7 (src 53, 56); the same advertiser has 'a huge Q4' (CEO, src 51). The lift is below 2025's 1.20 because Adobe sees holiday growth slowing to +6.7% from Q3's +10.4% (src 53). FY2027-29 built from the two demand engines (not disclosed separately; one revenue driver): revenue = installs x net revenue per install (10-Q MD&A: Q3 installs +2%, NRPI +55%; Q2 -2%/+58%; Q1 -18%/+93%; FY2025 +3%/+72%; src 47, 2, 3, 16), i.e. growth is pricing of deeper-funnel installs by Axon and new consumer advertisers, not install volume. SPLIT (estimate, not disclosed; CFO Q3 call: no split given, src 51): gaming ~84% / consumer ~16% of FY2026 revenue, triangulated from the Q3 call: total +55.5% y/y (src 46) with consumer 'triple digits' taken at ~+110% (low end; Kilian 2026-11-05) and gaming 'nearly 50%' taken at 47-49% puts consumer at ~14-18% of Q3-26 revenue (gaming +49% -> 14%, +48% -> 16%, +47% -> 18%), centre 16%; Q1 lower and the Q4 peak higher (src 51). The Q1-26 call's '$1 billion run rate a year ago' (src 49) is not stated as revenue or advertiser spend; APP reports net revenue ('net revenue dollars', gross spend near $20B annualized per analyst Benjamin Black (Deutsche Bank) recapping a CEO remark, vs ~$8.7B revenue, src 51), so it is not used for the split. Sensitivity below. GAMING: end market flat (mobile game IAP $82B, +1% in 2025, Sensor Tower, src 50); APP grows by share and per-install pricing. Q3-26 gaming grew 'nearly 50%' y/y with the next-generation model only partly rolled out; the rest of the transition is ahead but with no committed cadence (CEO, src 51). The CEO's earlier gaming expectation was 20-30% a year ('we've been way over those rates', Q1-26 call, src 49); the CEO now commits only to ~30% for the whole business and says gaming 'could' grow faster if the new model is optimized (src 51). Path (Kilian's 11-24 card pick 'Gaming at the 20% floor'): +20% a year FY2027-29, the bottom of management's earlier range, against a flat IAP market. CONSUMER (web/e-commerce): advertiser spend 'growing triple digits' y/y and 'double digits' q/q in Q3-26 (CFO, src 51); self-serve opened in June 2026, rolled out in sequence with mid-market first (Q1-26 and Q2-26 calls, src 49, 17); customers mostly Western, international effort not yet launched (src 49); new customers ~$70k a year with near-zero churn after 30 days (src 49); CEO Q3: 'really early', 'lightly penetrated', new-customer acquisition now a growth component, the new model helps most where data is sparse, 'exactly where our consumer vertical lives' (src 51); still slow to ramp: incrementality studies, SMB 'further into the future' (src 51). Path +50% / +40% / +30% (same pick): a step down from 2026's triple digits as the base grows, with a slow advertiser ramp (incrementality studies, Wells Fargo pixel 'false start', src 28); the Jefferies Q2 2026 survey of 30 e-commerce advertisers (APP 11% of their budgets, +169 bp; 2026 DTC ad spend +15%, src 63) supports the ramp but not a faster one. Total 10,455.2 / 12,948.3 / 15,819.6 (+24.8% / +23.8% / +22.2%). OUTSIDE CHECK: FY2027 sits at the Street: Zacks consensus $10.47B (10 estimates, 9.88-10.79B, src 60), Morgan Stanley $10.36B after the Q3 print (src 61; base case ~29% CAGR, bear ~15%), Bank of America +23% (Aug, src 62). The pre-pick path (gaming +30/25/20%, consumer +75/50/35%) put FY2027 9.8% above Zacks on management's words only. Consumer share 10% / 20% instead of 16%: -3.8% / +2.6% on value; with the 16% start consumer is ~20% / 24% / 26% of FY2027-29 revenue. Whole-business path FY2026-29 compounds at +23.6% a year, below management's 'roughly 30% annually over the long term' (src 51; that path is the first alternative). Quarters: y/y declining linearly within each year, solved to hit each year's total (Q2 seasonally weakest, Q4 peak, src 17); Q1-27 +7.6% q/q vs +11% in Q1-26 and +16% in Q1-25, as the consumer mix brings 'tougher Q1s' after Q4 (src 51). Alternatives: management's path (+16.4%) and faster consumer (+12.9%), judgment_alternatives.

EBITDA 2,038.5 = revenue 2,426.6 less cash costs 388.1, built from the Q3 10-Q cost lines ex SBC, D&A and transaction items (src 47: cost of revenue 240.8 - intangible amortization 13.3 - other D&A 7.4 = data center and payment processing 220.0, 10.07% of revenue after the serving optimizations the CEO and CFO describe (src 51); S&M 53.0, R&D 33.7, G&A 35.9 = opex 122.6). Q4: serving and processing at 10.07% of revenue (no further optimization assumed) = 244.4; +15.0 training compute (the CFO says the Q4 outlook includes higher data center cost for training new models, src 51; 15.0 = 0.6 pt of revenue, inside the 0-0.8 pt quarter-to-quarter moves in the compute share this year: 9.97% / 10.76% / 10.07% in Q1-Q3, src 3, 2, 47); opex +5% (128.7: marketing programs drove S&M +42% y/y in Q3, src 47, and the CEO is ramping new-customer acquisition and CTV, src 51). Incremental margin on Q3 81% (Q2->Q3 actual 87%, CFO, src 51); the guide ($1,995-2,025M, 84-85%) is the cross-check: +1.4% over its midpoint. FY2027-29 quarters = the 2026 margin of the same quarter (Q1 84.50%, Q2 83.89%, Q3 84.32%, Q4 84.01%): margins have held 83.9-84.5% for five quarters (Q4-25..Q4-26 guide), and the CFO's Q2-call 'low 80 percent' range (src 17) is overtaken by the Q4 guide of 84-85% (src 46). Flat is the midpoint of two real-world forces, not a trend fit. UP: Q2->Q3 incremental margin was ~87%, above the 84% average (CFO, src 51), and data center costs fell as a share of revenue (CEO and CFO, src 51). DOWN: model training investment is rising, CTV is in pilots and new-customer acquisition in consumer is being ramped (src 51), and the CFO: 'We manage this business to EBITDA dollars and free cash flow rather than to a margin percentage' (src 51), i.e. reinvest rather than let margin climb. The FY2027-29 level is Kilian's 11-24 card pick 'Hold at 2026 levels' (no source gives a margin figure for those years). Each 1pt of margin moves the research target ~1.3%.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Which FY2027-29 revenue path should APP's model use?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: Revenue is APP's one big driver: gaming (~84% of FY2026, an estimate; APP does not split it) plus consumer/e-commerce (~16%). The set books gaming +30/25/20% and consumer +75/50/35% for FY2027-29 (about +30% a year overall, in line with the CEO's 'roughly 30% annually over the long term'), with Q4 FY2026 now built from the same two engines at 2,426.6 (+2.0% over the guide midpoint). Q3 gaming grew 'nearly 50%' with the new model only partly rolled out and consumer grew triple digits, but the mobile game spending pool behind gaming is flat to down (Sensor Tower), management's earlier gaming range was 20-30% a year, and consumer advertisers ramp slowly (incrementality studies). Two evidence-based paths move the research target (12m) by more than 5%.

options.label: Booked path
options.reasoning: Gaming +30% in FY2027 is the top of management's earlier 20-30% range and already a big step down from ~48% in Q3 with the rollout unfinished; consumer +75% steps down from triple digits as the base grows. Whole business ~+30% a year, management's long-term aim.

options.label: Gaming at the 20% floor
options.reasoning: Gaming at the bottom of management's earlier 20-30% range every year against a flat in-app spending market (Sensor Tower $82B in 2025, +1%; top-10 Q3 2026 -3% q/q) and consumer cut to +50/40/30% on the slow-ramp evidence (Wells Fargo pixel 'false start').

options.label: Faster consumer
options.reasoning: Consumer +100/65/45%: CEO calls consumer 'lightly penetrated' with international not yet launched, and consumer spend grew double digits quarter over quarter in a non-peak Q3; gaming unchanged.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.recommendation: Decided by the owner: Gaming at the 20% floor
judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: It sits between the two evidence-based extremes: gaming already runs well above management's old range with the rollout still ahead, while consumer's ramp is real but slow; the booked path is a steep slowdown from today's ~55% growth, which keeps the base case moderately conservative.

Against that, the CFO says they manage to EBITDA dollars, not margin, while model training, CTV pilots and consumer customer acquisition ramp up. In Q1-Q3 2025 margins were 80.9-82.4%. Each point of margin moves the research target (12m) by about 1.3%.
